summary.en: Four small words join ideas: **and** adds (_I opened the window and sat down_), **but** shows a contrast (_It was sunny but cold_), **so** gives a result (_I was tired, so I went to bed_) and **because** gives a reason (_I went to bed because I was tired_). Each links two clauses, so each part has its own subject and verb.
summary.es: And suma, but contrasta, so da el resultado («así que») y because da la razón («porque»). Después de so y because va una frase completa, con sujeto y verbo.

form: **And** joins similar ideas: _We had coffee and talked for an hour._
**But** joins contrasting ideas, usually after a comma: _I like the flat, but it's expensive._
**So** + result, after a comma: _The shop was closed, so we went home._
**Because** + reason: _We went home because the shop was closed._ After **because of** use a noun: _because of the rain_.
**Because** can start a short answer: _Why are you late? Because the bus broke down._

uses.text: **Contrasting** → _He is very young, but he is a good manager._
**Saying what happened as a result** → _It was raining, so we stayed in._
**Giving the reason** → _I'm learning English because I want a better job._

note.es: Because va delante de la razón.

mistakes.wrong: I was ill, because I stayed at home.
mistakes.right: I was ill, so I stayed at home.

why.en: Staying at home is the result, so use so. Use because before the reason: I stayed at home because I was ill.
why.es: El resultado lleva so; la razón lleva because.

mistakes.wrong: Because I was ill. I stayed at home.
mistakes.right: Because I was ill, I stayed at home.

why.en: A because clause cannot stand alone before a main clause. Join the two with a comma or put because second.
why.es: La frase con because no puede quedar suelta: une las dos partes.

mistakes.wrong: I don't go out because of I'm tired.
mistakes.right: I don't go out because I'm tired.

why.en: Because of is followed by a noun. Before a clause use because.
why.es: Because of + nombre; because + frase completa.

mistakes.wrong: I wanted to call you, so I didn't have your number.
mistakes.right: I wanted to call you, but I didn't have your number.

why.en: The second idea is a contrast, not a result, so use but.
why.es: La segunda idea contrasta: usa but.

mistakes.wrong: I took my umbrella so it was raining.
mistakes.right: I took my umbrella because it was raining.

why.en: The rain is the reason, so use because. So would put the result after it.
why.es: La lluvia es la razón: because. So va delante del resultado.

examples.en: I went to the market and bought some fruit.
examples.es: Fui al mercado y compré fruta.

examples.en: The hotel was cheap, but it was very noisy.
examples.es: El hotel era barato, pero muy ruidoso.

examples.en: Our flight was late, so we missed the last train.
He didn't answer the phone because he was in a meeting.
examples.es: No contestó al teléfono porque estaba en una reunión.

examples.en: I'm tired, so I'm going to bed early tonight.
We wanted to go to the beach, but it was raining.
She stayed at home because she had a headache.
Why are you learning Spanish? Because I want to work in Madrid.
They cancelled the match because of the weather.
My brother speaks German and French, but he doesn't speak Italian.

practice.prompt: I like swimming, ___ I don't like running.

explanation.en: The two ideas contrast, so use but.

practice.prompt: It was very cold, ___ I put on my coat.

explanation.en: Putting on a coat is the result of the cold, so use so.

practice.prompt: She is happy ___ she passed her driving test.

explanation.en: Passing the test is the reason, so use because.

practice.prompt: We're staying at home tonight ___ it's raining heavily.

explanation.en: The rain is the reason for staying at home, so use because.
